**No blocking ambiguities. Proceeding to adversarial planning.**

The body is unusually complete (exact failing line, three reproduction
contexts, ranked fix options plus an explicit do-NOT). The context pass below
resolved every question I would otherwise have asked, and sharpened two claims
in the body.

## Context resolved

- **Failure reproduced first-hand on unmodified `main`** (repo root, branch
  `main`, target file byte-identical to `origin/main` — no local diff):
  `assert _ppid(detached_pid) == "1"` fails `'2887' == '1'`; file total
  **1 failed, 4 passed in 0.46s**. Matches the body exactly.
- **Reparent target confirmed live, not inferred.** `ps -o pid=,ppid=,comm= -p 2887`
  → `2887 1 systemd`, and my own session's ancestry walk terminates
  `... -> 2887 (systemd --user) -> 1`. So 2887 is the per-user `systemd`
  instance and is a genuine ancestor of the pytest process — exactly the
  `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` reparent path the body names. This closes #2112's
  explicit `unverified hypothesis — verify at plan time` ("miner-inferred from
  the assertion diff, not probed against the live process tree").
- **DUPLICATE FOUND: task #2112** (`daily-fix: setsid pin test env-brittle
  (subreaper ppid)`, `kind: infra`, `wf-fix`, `wf-fix-fp:4e505106423d`, filed
  2026-08-06, status `proposed`) targets the SAME assertion on the SAME file,
  and carries the canonical `workflow_fix_target:
  tests/test_workflow_setsid_detach_convention.py` Provenance line. Routing
  decision below; nothing is dropped.
- **Intermittency discrepancy between the two bodies is RESOLVED.** #2112
  frames the node as *intermittent* ("flake-hardening, not fix-the-red-node")
  on the strength of one green run at 2026-08-06T06:40Z; #2199 frames it as
  persistent. Both are right about their own observation and wrong about the
  general claim: the failure is **deterministic given the process ancestry**
  and **context-dependent across ancestries** — red wherever a subreaper
  ancestor exists (any Happy/Claude session, since they descend from
  `systemd --user`), green in an ancestry that reparents straight to PID 1
  (#2112's own compose-time cron context, which it already hypothesised).
  It is NOT load-flaky: my run was in isolation, single test file, 0.46 s, and
  #2199 independently reproduced it in isolation. This matters for the fix — a
  timing/retry hardening would be the wrong instrument.
- **The body's fleet-wide-impact claim is directionally right but overstated
  in one respect — corrected here for the plan.** The file is **not** a
  `tests/step9c_workflow_invariant_manifest.txt` member (109 entries, no
  `setsid` hit), so it is *not* selected on every Step 9c run. It IS selected
  via the selector's dependency arm for workflow-surface payloads:
  `select_step9c_tests.py --map-files` on a probe diff of
  `.claude/skills/issue/SKILL.md` + `.claude/rules/code-style.md` maps BOTH to
  `tests/test_workflow_setsid_detach_convention.py` (the test text-pins
  literals in both). So the tax lands on exactly the rounds that touch
  `SKILL.md` / `code-style.md` — the workflow-fix population, the
  highest-frequency infra traffic — rather than literally every round. The
  "permanently-red gate normalises waving through a real failure" argument
  survives this correction intact.
- **Mechanism is already durable project knowledge** (so no re-derivation
  needed at plan time): `.claude/agent-memory/implementer/reference_vm_subreaper_orphan_reparent.md`
  — "setsid orphans reparent to `systemd --user` (subreaper), not PID 1;
  `ppid==1` asserts fail environmentally", indexed in that agent's `MEMORY.md`.
- **Reuse sweep for an existing subreaper helper: none exists.** Repo-wide
  grep for `CHILD_SUBREAPER|subreaper|child_subreaper` across `*.py`/`*.md`/`*.sh`
  returns only prose (agent memory, the two task bodies, a codex-critic memory
  note) — no code helper to reuse, and no other test asserting a reparent
  target (`_ppid` appears only in this file; `tests/test_tick_triage.py` /
  `tests/test_autonomous_session_watch.py` use a monkeypatched `_proc_ppid`
  for unrelated tmux-ancestry walks). So the fix is local to this one file.
- **Blast radius is one assertion.** The other four cases in the file pass, and
  they cover the prose pins plus the primary `killpg`-survival mechanism. Only
  the line-124 "second kill vector" claim encodes the false environment
  assumption.
- **History:** the test landed 2026-07-30 in `ba8359381c` (filed under #1689),
  and the file has had no commit since — consistent with both bodies.

## Routing decision on the #2112 duplicate

Autonomous scope call, stated per the auto-continuation policy rather than
blocking: **execute the fix on #2199** (the task I was invoked on, and the one
carrying the stronger evidence base — deterministic repro, exact line, ranked
options with a do-NOT guard), and **fold #2112's added value into the plan**
rather than re-deriving it. #2112 contributes three things #2199 lacks: the
2026-08-05 gate-context sighting history on #1996 (two independent parks, fp
`4516c07c1164`), the green-at-06:40Z datapoint that pins the
context-dependence, and the acceptance bar `the node is reliably green on
pristine main in every execution context (gate tree, repo root, worktree,
cron)` — which is a strictly better deliverable statement than #2199's and
will be carried into the plan's acceptance criteria.

`#2112` will be set to `archived` with a pointer to #2199 once the fix lands
(not now — if this round fails, #2112 should remain live as the fallback
record). A dedup note is posted to #2112 immediately so no concurrent PM pass
or auto-dispatch picks it up mid-round.
